response.message:
I've drafted the end-to-end AWS pipeline. Synthetic devices send to AWS IoT Core, which feeds a replayable Kinesis stream. A validator checks events against a device registry and rejects unknown devices or invalid units, then a scorer deduplicates events, applies the late-event policy and calls a SageMaker endpoint. Each result is stored with its evidence and model version, and anomalies alert an operator through SNS.

**First local test:** we'd replay a fixed set of synthetic events through the validator and scorer, using a scripted fake model. That test can show:
- unknown devices and invalid units are rejected
- duplicate events produce exactly one result
- late and out-of-order events follow the policy
- replay after a disconnect recovers the missing results
- each anomaly result names its evidence and model version

It proves the pipeline's behaviour, not detection quality. Testing the real model needs held-out synthetic data, measured miss and false-alarm rates, and a reachable endpoint.

**Not yet covered:** the export's native code only covers part of this design. IoT Core, Kinesis, the SageMaker model and the scoring code still need engineering. Nothing has been deployed, and no region or account access has been approved.

Will your synthetic data include labelled anomalies we can train and score against, or should we start with an unsupervised detector?

proposal.title: AWS sensor anomaly detection pipeline (first sketch)
proposal.body: Scope: synthetic sensor events → IoT Core ingestion → Kinesis durable, replayable buffer → Lambda validation against a DynamoDB device registry (rejects to SQS) → validated Kinesis stream → Lambda scorer (idempotent dedup, late/out-of-order policy) → SageMaker AI anomaly endpoint → DynamoDB results with evidence and model version → SNS operator alert. Assumptions: region not selected; model type (supervised vs unsupervised) undecided; late-event window undecided; Kinesis retention period undecided. IoT Core, Kinesis, SageMaker and the scoring code have no native generator coverage and require engineering. Nothing is deployed or verified.

data.label: Synthetic device simulator
data.description: External synthetic telemetry generator outside the provisioning scope. Emits {deviceId, eventId, timestamp, metric, value, unit} over MQTT/TLS with per-device X.509 certificates, and buffers events locally while disconnected.

data.label: Device ingestion
data.description: Authenticates devices by certificate and routes telemetry through an IoT rule to Kinesis, unchanged. Preserves deviceId, timestamps and units, and adds the ingest time.

data.label: Raw telemetry buffer
data.description: Durable, ordered buffer partitioned by deviceId. Its retention window supports replay after disconnects or failures; the retention period is to be decided.

data.label: Event validator
data.description: Uses a Kinesis event source mapping with partial batch failure reporting. Rejects events from unknown devices and events whose units are invalid for the registered metric, plus malformed timestamps. Forwards valid events unchanged.

data.label: Device registry
data.description: The authoritative list of known devices, with the allowed metrics and units for each.

data.label: Rejected events
data.description: Holds rejected events with a rejection reason for operator inspection; nothing is silently dropped.

data.label: Validated telemetry
data.description: Validated events, partitioned by deviceId so each device's events stay in order for scoring.

data.label: Anomaly scorer
data.description: Deduplicates on deviceId+eventId with a conditional write, so duplicates produce one result. Applies the explicit late/out-of-order policy (window to be decided) and invokes the model endpoint. The response it writes includes the anomaly score, evidence features and the model version.

data.label: Anomaly model endpoint
data.description: Hosted anomaly model that returns a score and the model version. Supervised vs unsupervised is undecided. Local tests use a scripted mock, which proves nothing about detection quality.

data.label: Anomaly results
data.description: One result per deviceId+eventId: original timestamp and unit, score, evidence, model version and late-event flag.

data.label: Operator alert
data.description: Publishes one alert per anomalous result, including the device, time, evidence and model version.

data.label: Operator
data.description: The person who receives and triages anomaly alerts; outside the provisioning scope.

data.label: Pipeline monitoring
data.description: Tracks iterator age, rejection rate, scorer errors and alert volume to detect backlog and failures.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Bad events would otherwise create false anomalies.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Reject unknown device and invalid units"
requirementDrafts.statement: Events from unregistered devices or with units not allowed for the metric are rejected with a reason and never scored.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Kinesis and MQTT can deliver an event more than once, and duplicates would trigger duplicate alerts.
requirementDrafts.statement: Each deviceId+eventId produces exactly one result, even when the event is delivered more than once.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without an explicit policy, scoring is not reproducible.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Late and out-of-order telemetry follows an explicit policy"
requirementDrafts.statement: Late and out-of-order events are handled by an explicit, documented policy (acceptance window to be decided) and flagged in the result.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Data must not be lost during an outage; the retention period still needs to be decided.
requirementDrafts.statement: After a disconnection, buffered and retained telemetry can be replayed to produce the missing results without duplicating any.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Operators need evidence to triage alerts and auditors need the model version.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Anomaly output names evidence and model version"
requirementDrafts.statement: Every anomaly result and alert names its evidence (metrics and values) and the model version.

response.message:
No runtime tests have run yet, so this design is not validated. The emulation stopped before running any checks: 0 checks ran and 0 passed. An empty failures list here only means nothing was tested, not that the design is correct.

The first blocker is the IoT Core → Kinesis → validator → scorer path. It's the core of your pipeline, and none of our supported contracts implements it. The supported asynchronous pipeline (S3 → SQS → Lambda → DynamoDB) only counts words in documents. Swapping it in would shrink the scope to fit the generator, so we won't do that. Instead, the eight "implementation needed" gaps go to product engineering as native generators for IoT Core, Kinesis, the validator, the registry, the reject queue and the scorer. The fixed synthetic event set from the first local test can serve as the reproducer.

The simulator gap is a decision only you can make. It's an external system outside what we provision, so the plan needs to know whether it gets a device identity created in AWS or brings certificates you already manage.

So my question: should the device certificates for the synthetic simulator be created as part of this project, or do you already manage them somewhere else?
